steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a large bowl, combine the beef, onion, oatmeal, cornmeal, bread crumbs, salt, sugar, egg, tomato juice, water, barbecue sauce, 1/8 teaspoon liquid smoke and vinegar. Mix together thoroughly and place mixture into a lightly greased 9x5 inch loaf pan.
In a separate small bowl, combine the ketchup, brown sugar, mustard and 2 drops liquid smoke and mix thoroughly. Spread over the top of the meatloaf.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for approximately one hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Best Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: Oatmeal, cornmeal, and bread crumbs are all included here, along with barbecue sauce, liquid smoke, and vinegar for a unique glazed meatloaf.
raw_recipe.name: Mom's Best Meatloaf

review.reviewBody: Wow!! This is the best meatloaf I have ever had! I did have to make a few substitutions because of things I had in my pantry...I used balsamic vinegar (didn't have any regular), V8 juice for the tomato juice and tomato paste instead of ketchup. My husband raved about the wonderful taste and texture....we will definitely be enjoying this recipe again and again and again......

I have been looking for a moist meatloaf recipe for years.....I found it in this recipe! The only change I made was to omit the liquid smoke. I felt it was unnecessary to add this ingredient.
I cooked it in a loaf pan with a riser inside to lift the meat off the bottom to allow the grease to separate from the meatloaf. I also used 96% hamberger meat therefore again less fat.
You won't be disappointed. This is a keeper!

Made this for a funeral dinner. I cooked them in a muffin pan so they could easily be served. I also took the advise of another reviewer and used half of the bread crumbs, used tomato sauce instead of juice and eliminated the water. EVERYONE loved it. Thank you

I made it 99% to recipe. I changed the white vinegar to apple cider vinegar. I took all of the liquid ingredients and mixed on low in the blender then poured into the hamburger. After thoroughly mixing, I added the flour mixture. I did add about 1/2 cup more bread crumbs. It seemed very moist after mixing so I wanted to be sure it held together. It tuned out great. I loved the flavor. I worried about baking it uncovered but the sauce prevented it from drying out and nothing burned. Yay.

My family loved this (especially me) and I usually am not a big fan of meatloaf. I did not have tomato juice so i substituted tomato sauce. I also punched holes on the top before adding topping so that flavor of topping gets into the meat. I also cooked this on a large cookie sheet rather than a loaf pan so that the meat would cook more evenly throughout. Thanks for the fabulous recipe.

This is a great basic meatloaf recipe. It has become a family favorite. I often double the recipe and use two pounds of ground beef and 1 pound of hot Italian sausage. Instead of plain breadcrumbs, I incorporate those with Italian seasoning. These modifications add great flavor!
the only meatloaf we make, the only thing we do different is something that happened on accident. We double the sauce and mix half into the meat before we cook it. So good.

I made a few changes. 1. I used 1 lb of beef and 1 lb of ground pork. 2. I didn't read the instructions and mistakenly just added everything into the meat loaf. 3. I didn't add ketchup or tomato juice. I just used some tomato sauce in their place. 4. I just topped the meatloaf with ketchup. WELL...it came out really tasty! I will make this again!

Added a dash of Worcestershire sauce. Didn’t use liquid smoke, corn meal or mustard. Substituted balsamic for the white vinegar. It came out delicious but did need more than an hour to cook. I’ll make it again!

I've made this several times with excellent outcomes. Last night I made it again and wanted to reduce the cost (as I didn't have most of the ingredient in my kitchen). As I never use cornmeal for any other of my recipes I left it out. Instead of tomato juice I used a small can of tomato paste (save me a dollar). I used Jack Daniel's BBQ sauce, flavored breadcrumbs, and doubled the sauce recipe. The meatloaf came out moist but not mushy, absolutely perfect texture

Fantastic flavor, I did made some changes, like adding 1/2 a pound of ground veal an a 1/4 pound of ground pork. I also cooked it cover for and hour and uncover for 40 minutes. It was extremely moist but not so much that it felt apart. I also added one garlic.

The flavour of this was great, but the texture was off. The mix was a bit wet, so I contemplated messing with it a bit before baking but decided to stick to the recipe. I should have added more breadcrumbs, because once cooked it was still a bit loose and fell apart a bit as I took it out of the loaf tin. Will play around with the texture, since I loved the flavour, and see if I can get it right.

I enjoyed the recipe. I used Worcester sauce instead of liquid smoke and used the liquid off of diced tomatoes instead of tomato juice. (I have to cut down on sodium as much as possible.) The flavor was great. I'll be making another soon.
This is my meatloaf go to. My wife is allergic to mustard so I substitute cayenne. Used maple sugar just because I have it. Great recipe!
This is my meatloaf go to. My wife is allergic to mustard so I substitute cayenne. Used maple sugar just because I have it. Great recipe!

This is the only meatloaf recipe I use now! The only change I make is replacing the tomato juice for a small can of tomato sauce. This makes it less wet and hold together better. The liquid smoke gives it great flavor and the sweet and tangy sauce on top is perfect. I serve it with mashed potatoes and corn.

I've used this as a working meatloaf recipe for years.
I usually add more veggies; namely chopped red/green peppers and garlic. I tweak the seasoning to comply with my dietary goals, and usually increase the topping.
It is always moist and flavorful.

I did not have the liquid smoke and my sweetie says liquid smoke gives him terrible heartburn so it is just as well. With all that said, this recipe is the best I have ever had. He said it is the second best he has ever had-next to the one he grew up on. :) Of course....
this tastes too much like candy so the kids liked it, I did not.
Been searching a very long time for a meatloaf recipe that was good enough to use as a regular standby. I think this is it! Delicious....& even more so leftover.
